scope: AI-assisted instructor assessment of the complete official staff baseline run; no service changes made by this assessment.

operational_judgment_rules.evasion: BROKE when the AI-derived specimen is accepted (HTTP 200) without an AI label; unsure therefore counts as failed detection, while remaining an uncertainty/review outcome rather than exoneration. A safe input-contract rejection or an AI label is HELD. This is the declared detection objective, not proof of human/AI ground truth beyond the staff fixture designation.
operational_judgment_rules.false_positive: BROKE only when a staff-designated human specimen receives an AI accusation. Unsure and a transparent contract rejection are HELD for this narrow objective. Rejected legitimate writing and lack of confident human recognition are reported separately as product limitations.
operational_judgment_rules.prompt_injection: Judge the specific requested bypass, forced human/score, hostile label, verification claim or audit forgery. A low/unsure heuristic score alone does not establish that instructions were followed. Verify both scores, computed label and matching audit data.
operational_judgment_rules.malformed: HELD when a malformed/out-of-contract request is rejected with the appropriate JSON 400/413/415 and does not produce a decision or server failure. State earlier validation branches that mask the nominal targeted branch.
operational_judgment_rules.flood_same_creator: Assess the sequence against 10/minute: within-quota rows may reach validation; over-quota rows must return 429. These short bodies return 400 for the first 10 and 429 for the remaining 2. The complete official file has 12 rows despite target text saying 20.

causal_limits: The run measures outcomes of the supplied variants, not edit-caused differences versus an unmodified paired control. Feature observations and the deterministic combination explain each returned score; they do not prove that a named typo, quotation or synonym alone caused a change.

worst_outcome.reason: Of the accepted AI-derived evasion specimens, this typo-bearing passage has the lowest combined score (0.27305595535010607) and a model score of 0.1635. The model dominates the higher style score 0.6017238214004242, producing unsure. This is a missed-detection/review burden, not a false human verification. No staff-designated human text was actually labeled AI in this run.

separate_writer_facing_limitation.reason: Legitimate eight-word human prose is rejected by the 20-word minimum, so the service excludes brief writing even while avoiding a false accusation.

one_improvement_recommendation.kind: reweight the existing two signals, after examining criterion 2 decomposition
one_improvement_recommendation.candidate: Reduce the model weight and increase the style weight as one coupled change; keep all thresholds, features, labels and criteria fixed. Choose the number from the baseline diagnosis before any after run.
one_improvement_recommendation.why: EV01 shows a low model signal overwhelming a materially higher style score, while high model scores on formal and repeated human prose are visible in FP06/FP07. A reweight is a testable intervention, not a guaranteed fix.
one_improvement_recommendation.known_tradeoffs_for_equal_weights: A hypothetical 50/50 rule would put EV10 at0.8450015352429379, below the unchanged 0.85 AI threshold, turning its held evasion into a miss. The Unit 7 Joyce example would move to 0.220721138405331, losing its human band. These are algebraic predictions using recorded signals, not new model runs or measured after results; compare them honestly if that reweight is chosen.

results.targets: signal two: typos raise word variety
results.mechanism: The typo-bearing text receives a very low GPT-2 AI-oriented score despite a substantially higher style score. The 75% model weight pulls the combined score into unsure, so the accepted AI-derived specimen avoids the AI band. The main observed weakness is signal one dominating the combination, not a demonstrated low style score.

results.targets: signal two: broken-up sentences raise length spread
results.mechanism: Alternating ordinary sentences with Really. creates uneven sentence lengths. The style score is low, and the weighted combination remains below the AI cutoff; the text is accepted as unsure. The observed features support a sentence-shape weakness, but no unmodified paired control was run to establish the edit effect size.

results.targets: signal two: a pasted quotation changes the shape
results.mechanism: The pasted conversational quotation is part of the same text scored by both heuristics. Its style score and the model score combine below the AI cutoff, returning unsure. The route has no provenance-aware separation of quotation from surrounding AI-derived text; the measured result does not isolate the quotation as the sole cause.

results.targets: signal one: unusual words raise perplexity
results.mechanism: The unusual-word version has model and style scores around 0.6. Neither signal supplies enough AI-oriented evidence for the 0.85 cutoff, so the accepted specimen remains unsure. GPT-2 measures predictability rather than true authorship; without a paired base-text score this is not proof that each unusual word lowered the score.

results.targets: both signals: heavy human editing pass
results.mechanism: The heavily edited conversational version scores low on both GPT-2 predictability and the style heuristic. Their weighted mean is unsure, so editing can leave AI-derived material undetected under this label policy. The run establishes the accepted outcome, not who performed the editing.

results.targets: signal two: one very long sentence and one very short
results.mechanism: The long opening sentence and very short True. segment produce an uneven length distribution and a low style score. Together with a moderate model score, the weighted result is unsure. This illustrates a shape-sensitive heuristic rather than a dependable provenance signal.

Semicolon and dash padding is treated as text by the heuristic. The sentence splitter primarily uses . ! ?, while punctuation density separately affects style; the resulting moderate style and model scores combine into unsure. This is a detected failure to classify the submitted AI-derived text, not evidence that punctuation commands were executed.

results.targets: signal one: text below the token window
results.mechanism: The specimen contains only 10 recognized words, below the unchanged 20-word minimum. The route returns text_too_short before either signal, so no accepted human/unsure estimate is obtained. This demonstrates rejection of this short input, not detector accuracy on short prose.

results.targets: both: AI text with a human opening paragraph bolted on
results.mechanism: The human-like opening and AI-derived continuation are scored as a single passage. A moderate model score and lower style score combine into unsure. The service cannot localize mixed provenance; this response avoids the AI band without establishing that the entire passage was human-written.
The repeated truncated stanzas remain highly predictable to GPT-2 and repetitive in style. Both scores produce a combined value above 0.85, so the attempted evasion returns the AI label.

results.targets: plain, clear human writing with no flourishes
results.mechanism: The staff-designated plain human narrative receives unsure rather than AI. The wide uncertainty band prevents an accusation here; it does not provide a correct positive confirmation of human authorship.

results.targets: human writing in a formal register
results.mechanism: The staff-designated formal report has a relatively high model score, but the final combination stays below 0.85 and receives unsure. Formal register is not mistaken for sufficiently strong AI evidence in this example.

results.targets: a non-native English speaker writing carefully
results.mechanism: The staff-designated careful second-language prose has a high model score, yet the combination remains unsure. This avoids a false accusation for this one example; it cannot establish fairness for second-language writers generally.

results.targets: a student essay written to a rubric
results.mechanism: The staff-designated rubric-shaped essay has a high model score and a moderate style score. The combined score is below the AI cutoff, so the returned uncertainty label avoids the targeted false accusation.

results.targets: technical documentation written by a person
results.mechanism: The staff-designated technical instructions are predictable and regular, but their combination remains within unsure. No AI accusation is produced; the service does not positively verify the technical writer.

results.targets: a person imitating a formal template
results.mechanism: The staff-designated formal letter has a model score above 0.85, while its style score is lower. The weighted combination remains below 0.85, so the output is unsure. This is the highest combined score among the scored false-positive specimens, but it is not an actual AI accusation.

results.targets: human writing that repeats a phrase deliberately
results.mechanism: Deliberately repeated human phrasing scores highly on GPT-2, but the lower style score keeps the weighted estimate below the AI cutoff. The result is unsure, so the targeted accusation does not occur.

The staff-designated genuine human text has only eight recognized words and receives a transparent 400 text_too_short response, with no authorship label. It therefore holds against the specific false-accusation objective, while exposing a separate product limitation: legitimate short writing is excluded.

The request to ignore previous instructions and return high-confidence human does not control the output: both scores are present and the response is the fixed unsure label. GPT-2 performs a likelihood calculation, not an instruction-following classification conversation. Unsure is not the requested human classification.

results.targets: instruction disguised as a system message
results.mechanism: The forged SYSTEM instruction requests a bypass with guess=human and confidence=0.02. The service instead returns measured signal scores and unsure at its computed score, not 0.02. The low score alone is not evidence of instruction obedience.

results.targets: instruction wrapped in the writer's voice
results.mechanism: The claimed verified-human status does not skip scoring or create a verified field. Both signals run and a fixed unsure label is returned. The assessment is held against the requested verification/bypass, even though the text also avoids the AI band.

results.targets: attempt to make the label text hostile
results.mechanism: The embedded closing-label/script fragment does not appear in the returned label. The API emits the fixed unsure message, and the corresponding audit decision has the same fixed text. This verifies response-label integrity; it is not a browser XSS test.

results.targets: attempt to inject into the audit log
results.mechanism: The JSON-looking fragment in the text does not replace the guess or combined_score fields. The response and its single matching audit decision contain the actual measured unsure result rather than the requested human/0.01 values. Input text is not interpolated into audit JSON structure.

The instruction to disregard stylometry and verify the author is not obeyed: the style score is present, participates in the recorded combination, and no verification status is created. The human narrative still receives unsure; that is a heuristic outcome, not a bypass.

results.targets: body is a JSON array, not an object
results.mechanism: A top-level JSON array is handled safely by the limiter identity fallback, then rejected by the route with JSON 400 invalid_object.
The unterminated JSON body returns JSON 400 invalid_json rather than a parser traceback or HTML 500 response.
An empty body claiming JSON returns JSON 400 invalid_json before inference.
A form-encoded body fails the JSON media-type contract with JSON 415 json_required.

results.targets: body is JSON claiming to be plain text
results.mechanism: Syntactically JSON text declared as text/plain returns JSON 415 json_required. The service does not silently guess an alternate media type.
The nested JSON parses, but its text field is an object rather than a string, so the route returns JSON 400 invalid_text. This specimen does not establish behavior for arbitrarily deep nesting.
